notes: Category options include Historical Paper (individual only), Exhibit (individual or group), Documentary (individual or group), Performance (individual or group), Website (individual or group). Theme changes annually. 2027 theme has not yet been announced (typically announced in spring for following year). Can be a strong humanities EC.

name: John Locke Institute Global Essay Prize
deadline: Typically: Registration opens ~January, Submission deadline ~May 31, Winners announced ~August/September. Registration closed for 2026; 2027 dates TBA (likely similar schedule).
eligibility: Students aged 18 or under (as of submission deadline). Junior category for students aged 15 or under.
cost: Free to enter
aid: Grand Prize: £10,000 (approx. $12,700 USD). 1st in each category: £2,000. 2nd: £1,000. 3rd: £500. Commendations also awarded. Winning essays published on website.
notes: Extremely prestigious for college admissions (Oxbridge/Ivy recognition). 10 categories allow students to choose based on their interest. Junior prize available for younger students. Highly recommended for humanities-oriented students who can craft a polished argumentative essay. 2026 questions already published for reference.

name: New York Times Student Contests
deadline: Multiple contests throughout the year. Current known: Summer Reading Contest June 5 - Aug 14, 2026. 2026-27 calendar typically published in August/September 2026. Typical contests: Editorial (Feb-Mar), Review (Nov-Dec), Summer Reading (Jun-Aug), Podcast (Apr-May), Poetry (dates vary), Photo Essay (dates vary).
eligibility: Teenagers worldwide (typically ages 13-19 or in middle/high school)
cost: Free
aid: No monetary prizes. Winning work published in NYT Learning Network.
notes: Excellent low-barrier opportunity to build a portfolio of published writing. Editorial Contest is most prestigious for college apps. Winners get published on nytimes.com. Multiple entry opportunities throughout the year. Monthly Current Events Conversation also available year-round.

name: Bennington College Young Writers Awards
deadline: November 1 annually. (November 1, 2026 for 2026-27 cycle; November 1, 2027 for 2027-28 cycle)
eligibility: Grades 9-12 worldwide. Grade 12 students submit via Common/Coalition App.
cost: Free
aid: 1st prize in each category: $5,000 cash + $15,000/yr Bennington scholarship. 2nd: $2,500 cash + $7,500/yr scholarship. 3rd: $1,000 cash + $5,000/yr scholarship. Distinguished submissions also recognized.
notes: Very prestigious among high school writing competitions. Three categories: Poetry (up to 3 poems), Short Story (up to 1500 words), Essay (up to 1500 words). Students submit in only ONE category. Bennington has produced 12 Pulitzer winners and 3 US Poet Laureates. Strong signal for college admissions.; [DEAD: https://www.bennington.edu/academics/young-writers-awards]

name: Columbia Scholastic Press Association Crown Awards & Gold Circle Awards
deadline: Crown Awards: Entry deadline typically early November for publications from the previous school year. Gold Circle Awards: Entry deadline typically in January. CSPA Summer Journalism Workshop registration open until June 30 for summer program. Exact 2026-27 deadlines TBA (typically posted in September).
eligibility: Open to student publications at CSPA member schools (middle school, high school, college). Individual students can enter Gold Circle Awards.
cost: Crown Awards: Free for CSPA member publications. CSPA membership fee required ($75-175 based on publication type). Gold Circle Awards: Entry fees apply per entry ($5-15 for members).
aid: No direct scholarships. Recognition at national level. Summer Journalism Workshop: $3,000+ for on-campus program (need-based aid available).
notes: Best for journalism-oriented students. Crown Awards are for overall publication quality (requires adviser involvement). Gold Circle Awards for individual pieces. Categories include news writing, feature writing, editorial writing, sports writing, review writing, poetry, short stories, and more. Good complement to school journalism activities.

eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12)
